title: Hacker, pack your bags!
statementMd:
It's well known that the best way to distract from something is to do one's favourite thing. Job is such a thing for Leha.

So the hacker began to work hard in order to get rid of boredom. It means that Leha began to hack computers all over the world. For such zeal boss gave the hacker a vacation of exactly $*x*$ days. You know the majority of people prefer to go somewhere for a vacation, so Leha immediately went to the travel agency. There he found out that $*n*$ vouchers left. $*i*$-th voucher is characterized by three integers $*l*_{*i*}$, $*r*_{*i*}$, $*cost*_{*i*}$ — day of departure from Vičkopolis, day of arriving back in Vičkopolis and cost of the voucher correspondingly. The duration of the $*i*$-th voucher is a value $*r*_{*i*} - *l*_{*i*} + 1$.

At the same time Leha wants to split his own vocation into two parts. Besides he wants to spend as little money as possible. Formally Leha wants to choose exactly two vouchers $*i*$ and $*j*$ $(*i* ≠ *j*)$ so that they don't intersect, sum of their durations is **exactly** $*x*$ and their total cost is as minimal as possible. Two vouchers $*i*$ and $*j*$ don't intersect if only at least one of the following conditions is fulfilled: $*r*_{*i*} < *l*_{*j*}$ or $*r*_{*j*} < *l*_{*i*}$.

Help Leha to choose the necessary vouchers!

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*x*$ $(2 ≤ *n*, *x* ≤ 2·10^{5})$ — the number of vouchers in the travel agency and the duration of Leha's vacation correspondingly.

Each of the next $*n*$ lines contains three integers $*l*_{*i*}$, $*r*_{*i*}$ and $*cost*_{*i*}$ $(1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ 2·10^{5}, 1 ≤ *cost*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9})$ — description of the voucher.

## Output

Print a single integer — a minimal amount of money that Leha will spend, or print $- 1$ if it's impossible to choose two disjoint vouchers with the total duration **exactly** $*x*$.

## Note

In the first sample Leha should choose first and third vouchers. Hereupon the total duration will be equal to $(3 - 1 + 1) + (6 - 5 + 1) = 5$ and the total cost will be $4 + 1 = 5$.

In the second sample the duration of each voucher is $3$ therefore it's impossible to choose two vouchers with the total duration equal to $2$.
statementZhMd:
众所周知，转移对某件事的注意力的最佳方式，就是去做自己喜欢的事情。对于 Leha 来说，工作就是这样一件事。

于是，这位黑客开始努力工作，以摆脱无聊。也就是说，Leha 开始入侵全世界的计算机。由于他的热情，老板奖励了他恰好 $*x*$ 天的假期。众所周知，大多数人更喜欢在假期去某个地方，因此 Leha 立即前往旅行社。在那里，他得知还剩下 $*n*$ 张旅行券。第 $*i*$ 张旅行券由三个整数 $*l*_{*i*}$、$*r*_{*i*}$、$*cost*_{*i*}$ 表示，分别代表离开 Vičkopolis 的日期、返回 Vičkopolis 的日期以及旅行券的价格。第 $*i*$ 张旅行券的持续时间为 $*r*_{*i*} - *l*_{*i*} + 1$。

同时，Leha 想把自己的假期分成两部分。此外，他希望花费尽可能少的钱。具体来说，Leha 想要选择恰好两张不同的旅行券 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$（$*i* ≠ *j*$），使得它们互不重叠、持续时间之和**恰好**为 $*x*$，并且总费用尽可能小。两张旅行券 $*i*$ 和 $*j*$ 互不重叠，当且仅当以下条件至少有一个成立：$*r*_{*i*} < *l*_{*j*}$ 或 $*r*_{*j*} < *l*_{*i*}$。

请帮助 Leha 选择所需的旅行券！

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*x*$（$2 ≤ *n*, *x* ≤ 2·10^{5}$）——旅行社中的旅行券数量以及 Leha 假期的持续时间。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含三个整数 $*l*_{*i*}$、$*r*_{*i*}$ 和 $*cost*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *l*_{*i*} ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ 2·10^{5}, 1 ≤ *cost*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$）——一张旅行券的描述。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——Leha 将要花费的最少金额；如果无法选择两张互不重叠且总持续时间**恰好**为 $*x*$ 的旅行券，则输出 $- 1$。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Leha 应该选择第一张和第三张旅行券。此时总持续时间为 $(3 - 1 + 1) + (6 - 5 + 1) = 5$，总费用为 $4 + 1 = 5$。

在第二个样例中，每张旅行券的持续时间都是 $3$，因此不可能选择两张旅行券，使它们的总持续时间等于 $2$。
